transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

On a Bosch WAN28281GB, E18 means the machine isn’t draining water properly. It has stopped to prevent flooding or damage.

Common causes are:

• A blocked pump filter (coins, lint, hair grips, small clothing items)
• A kinked or blocked drain hose
• A blocked sink/waste pipe connection
• Less commonly, a faulty drain pump

What to do:

1. Switch the washer off and unplug it.
2. Wait if the wash was hot — the water may be very hot.
3. Put towels and a shallow tray under the small service flap at the bottom front of the machine.
4. If present, use the little emergency drain hose behind the flap to drain the water slowly into a container.
• If there is no hose, very carefully loosen the pump-filter cap a little at a time to let water out.
5. Once empty, fully remove the pump filter, clean away debris, and check that the pump impeller behind it can move (don’t force it).
6. Refit the filter tightly, check the drain hose is not squashed or kinked, then try a Drain or Spin programme.

Do not try to force the door open while there is still water in the drum.

If the filter and hose are clear but E18 returns, or you hear the pump humming but no water moves, the drain pump or plumbing connection may need attention from a Bosch engineer or appliance repairer.

Thanks, I've done all that. I drained it through the little hose into a baking tray, which took several trays, and the water was grey and a bit smelly. The pump filter had a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus lots of fluff. The impeller was slightly notchy and then turned freely, and the drain hose looks fine and isn't kinked. I ran a drain/spin programme afterwards and it drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spins normally. The floor got a little wet while I was doing the filter, but there's no burning smell and no water near the socket. Is there anything else I should do?

That sounds like you’ve found and cleared the likely cause. A sock, hair grip and fluff around the filter can easily trigger E18, and the fact that it now drains quickly and spins normally is reassuring.

A few sensible final checks:

1. Make sure the pump filter is fully seated
• Recheck it is screwed in straight and firmly by hand (not cross-threaded).
• Wipe around the filter flap and check for drips over the next hour or two.

2. Dry the floor and check nearby areas
• Mop up all visible water.
• If water could have run underneath the machine, leave the area ventilated and check again later.
• Since there is no water near the socket and no burning smell, it is unlikely to be an electrical issue, but don’t use the machine if you see water around the plug/socket or notice tripping, sparking, or a hot/burning smell.

3. Run a short empty rinse or drum-clean cycle
• The grey, smelly water was likely old wash water sitting in the pump/filter area, combined with detergent residue and bacteria.
• An empty rinse, or ideally a hot maintenance wash (following Bosch’s guidance for your detergent/type of cleaner), will flush out any remaining residue. You can use a washing-machine cleaner if you have one.

4. Do the next normal load while you are nearby
• Check that it fills, washes, drains and spins without an E18 code or leaks from the filter area.
• A little initial pump noise after clearing an obstruction can be normal; persistent grinding, loud rattling, or another drainage fault is not.

Going forward, checking the pump filter every couple of months — and checking pockets for hair grips, coins, tissues etc. — should help prevent a repeat.
